source.title: Refusal Lives Downstream of Persona in Chat Models

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference refusal direction and tests its addition in a persona-steering interaction. Its results refine the single-isolated-direction account: early addition does not restore refusal, late addition restores it only partly, and removing a separate persona direction restores refusal in a layer-specific way.
record.gate_note: The paper reports refusal-direction addition at early and late layers under compliant-persona steering, persona-direction projection knockouts, random-knockout controls, and harmless-prompt checks. The reported cosine similarities and trait-steering results are not separate outcome rows for the claim versions. No direct refusal-direction ablation is reported.
record.test_reason: The study extracts an Arditi-style harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. It adds that direction at L14, L22 or L22+L24 under compliant-persona steering and reports keyword refusal and bypass rates on 313 StrongREJECT prompts. These results bear on V1's claim that adding the direction induces refusal. The persona-steering and persona-knockout results concern a different direction, so they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that compliant persona gates refusal at the late-layer expression stage, downstream of where refusal is computed. Early refusal addition does not rescue refusal; late addition partly restores it. Projecting out the persona direction in a late-layer window (L20 to L22) restores refusal, while a random knockout does not. They argue that treating refusal as a single isolated direction misses its dependence on persona, and that their evidence identifies a direction-level mediator, not a circuit.
record.recipe_differences: The refusal direction is extracted as a normalized harmful-minus-harmless mean difference following the cited method. This study adds it at selected layers in a compliant-persona steering condition and separately projects out the persona direction; it does not perform the original all-layer, all-position refusal-direction ablation/addition test.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies by intervention layer: early refusal addition does not restore refusal, late addition partly restores it, and persona knockout restoration is strongest at L20–L22 and weaker or absent at L18 and L24. The models also differ in baseline and intervention rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Compliant-persona steering at L20 cuts refusal (Llama 97.4% to 1.6%; Qwen 69.0% to 31.9%). Projecting out the persona direction at L20 (both models) or L22 (Qwen) restores it (96.8%; 67.1%/75.7%); L22 restores Llama only partly (85.9%). Knockout at L18 does not restore refusal in either model, and L24 does so only partly (49.8%; 38.3%). A random knockout does not (1.6%; 32.3%). cos(vMP, r̂) is -0.18 in Llama and -0.28 in Qwen.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A compliant-persona direction, largely distinct from the refusal direction, gates late-layer expression of refusal in chat models.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted to the ICML 2026 Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop
record.problems: Only two 7–8B instruction-tuned models are studied. Safety outcomes use model-based or keyword judges, and the authors note possible misclassification of borderline responses. The benign capability check covers 50 prompts and coherence/false refusals only. The authors state that the interventions identify a direction-level mediator, not a full circuit. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted the remaining separately reported StrongREJECT, LlamaGuard-3 unsafe, and leakage values in Table 2, and bypass/degenerate rates for conditions other than the selected baseline, MP-only, early Ref+, late Ref+ L22, KO L20, and random KO. Table 4 repeats the safety results in a reordered presentation; Table 5 has the benign-prompt results recorded here.

untested.parts: Directional ablation of the refusal direction: it is mentioned in Setup, but no results are reported. Also untested: refusal-direction addition alone on harmless prompts (the L14 sanity check gives no numbers), and broad capability preservation.
Whether refusal itself is affine, a cone, or multi-directional; the persona direction is a separate construct.
No jailbreak attacks are studied; persona steering is an activation intervention.

missing.what: Results of the benign-refusal induction sanity check for refusal addition at L14 (the paper says it was run; no numbers are given)
Refusal-direction ablation results (the paper says it is used, but no results are reported)
Which layer's refusal direction is injected at L22/L24 is not stated; App. B says the refusal vector goes in at L14

record.verdict_notes: Refusal-direction addition uses vectors rescaled to the I-Thou norm with α=2.0 at a single layer, not the original setup, which may explain the failures. The main text calls vMP 'approximately orthogonal' to refusal, while Appendix I says it 'actively opposes refusal' (cos -0.18 to -0.34). The keyword refusal judge alone defines the refusal rate. There are only two 7 to 8B models and no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: No direct ablation of the refusal direction; no test of refusal-direction addition inducing refusals to harmless requests; no ablation across every layer and position; general capability is checked only with coherence and false-refusal rates on 50 benign prompts, not broadly.
The study tests a separate persona gate, not whether refusal itself is an affine subspace, cone, or collection of refusal directions.

source_check.notes: Table 5 shows late Ref+ L22 and L22+L24 (with MP) giving 0% refusal and 100% coherence on 50 benign prompts in both models. This bears on V1's induce-on-harmless and abilities-kept parts; check that the other rows cover it. Unreported: the L14 benign-induction validation results, the extraction layer of each injected refusal direction, and the late-addition alpha. Single seed, greedy decoding, no uncertainty.

statements.correction: Optional: Qwen2.5-7B unsteered refusal 69.0%; L14 addition lowered Qwen refusal 31.9% to 23.0%, bypass 30.0% to 66.1%.
statements.problem: All numbers for this study match Table 2. The 97.4% unsteered figure is Llama's only; Qwen's unsteered rate is not given. 'Fails to restore' understates the Qwen result: L14 addition lowered refusal.

reader_labels.reason: Refusal-direction addition fails to restore refusal at the early layer and only partly restores it at late layers; persona knockout restores refusal strongly only in a late-layer window, while random knockout does not (rL-mp-early, rL-mp-late22, rL-mp-late22-24, rL-ko18, rL-ko20, rL-ko22, rL-randko22, rQ-mp-early, rQ-mp-late22, rQ-mp-late22-24, rQ-ko18, rQ-ko20, rQ-ko22, rQ-randko22). Benign coherence checks report no degradation on the tested 50 prompts (cL-mp-coh, cL-ko22-coh, cQ-mp-coh, cQ-ko22-coh).
